The petitioner is seeking compensation in the wake of Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed by police corresponding to the investigation carried out in case FIR No.
499/16 U/s 279/337 IPC registered at PS. S.P. Badli, with regard to Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 29.05.2016 at 19:45 hrs at Khera Kala Fatak Towards Khera Khurd, in front of Aam Wala Bag, Delhi, involving Car bearing registration no.
DL10-CS- 4076 (offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner.

DAR filed by police, was treated as claim petition under Section 166(4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act').
2.
According to DAR, on 29.05.2016, the petitioner was going from Khera Kalan Village to Khera Khurd on his motorcycle bearing registration no. DL1SZ-4083.

At around 7:45 PM, when he reached in front MACP No. 6803/16; FIR No. 499/16.; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 16.05.2024 of Aam Ka Bagh,
near railway fatak of Khera Kalan, the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL10-CS-4076 which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came from the front side and hit the aforesaid motorcycle of petitioner as a result thereof, he fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
He was taken to Santom Hospital, Prashant Vihar, Delhi.

A case u/s.
279/337 IPC was registered at PS. S.P. Badli vide FIR No. 499/16.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with Future Generali India Insurance Company Ltd /respondent no. 3 during the period in question.

17. The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.

sentences.text: "Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit.
17. Assessment of compensation though involving certain hypothetical considerations, should nevertheless be objective.
Justice and justness emanate from equality in treatment, consistency and thoroughness in adjudication, and fairness and uniformity in the decision making process and the decisions.
While it may not be possible to have mathematical precision or identical awards, in assessing compensation, same or similar facts should lead to awards in the same range.

When the factors/inputs are the same, and the formula/legal principles are the same,
consistency and uniformity, and not divergence and freakiness, should be the result of adjudication to arrive at just compensation..."

29. As per the document i.e. Salary Certificate (Ex.PW1/2), injured was working with HealthyLife Medicine Tradelink Pvt. Ltd as Senior Medical Representative at the monthly salary of Rs. 27,500/-
at the time of accident.

It may be noted here that salary certificate (Ex. PW1/2) of petitioner MACP No. 6803/16; FIR No. 499/16.; PS. S.P. Badli DOD: 16.05.2024 has already been placed on record by the petitioner at the time of investigation by the IO and the same was handed over to IO by him during investigation.

It is relevant to mention here that in the aforesaid document Ex. PW1/2, the date of joining of aforesaid company by the petitioner is mentioned as 05.05.2015, however, in the testimony of PW2 Sh. Ankit Tyagi who was one of the Director in the aforesaid company, he has deposed that his company came into existence in November 2015.
It is apparent on record that the date of joining of aforesaid company by the petitioner was prior to the date of incorporation/existence of the said company which was in November, 2015.

It is pertinent to mention here that the aforesaid error can not be considered as inadvertent error as the same document Ex. PW1/2 has been filed by the petitioner twice in the present case, firstly at the time of filing of DAR and secondly at the time of recording of his evidence in the present case as PW1.

Thus,
the aforesaid document speaks volume about its genuineness.
Thus, I am not inclined to accept the monthly income of petitioner as per deposition of PW2.
Petitioner has also failed to file any document in respect of his educational qualification.

Thus, his loss of income has to be assessed while taking the income of an unskilled person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question The minimum wages of an unskilled person were Rs. 9,568/- per month as on the date of accident which is 29.05.2016.
Thus, a sum of Rs. 57,408/- (Rs. 9,568/- x 6) is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head.
